hook.line: Don Hernando has had enough of Tomás wandering off in the middle of a crisis. He does not say please. He just says what is going to happen.

examples.en: You will do as I say.

examples.es: Ustedes harán lo que les diga.
examples.en: You all will do as I say.

rule:
Spanish can give an order as a plain statement. Say *tú* and the present: *tú te quedas aquí*. Or use the future of *tú*: *harás lo que te diga*.

There is no room to say no, so it is blunter than *quédate aquí*. English does the same with "you stay here".

Use it with children, with people who work for you, or as a joke among friends. With a stranger, it is rude.

It sits at the bottom of the courtesy ladder.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the present or future used as a command, instead of the imperative.

options: You are staying here, I hear.
I will do what you tell me.
You did what I told you.
You will do as I say.

readAndPick.es: Ustedes harán lo que les diga.
options: You (one person) will do as I say.
You all will do as I say.
They will do as I say.
You will do what I tell you, understood?
Will you do what I tell you, if you like?
I will do what you tell me, understood?

readAndPick.es: Tú llamas a Vale ahora mismo.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Tú ___ aquí.* (te quedas or quédate)
yourTurn.why: This order is a plain statement with *tú* and the present, not an imperative.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, as a firm order to a friend: You sit over there.
yourTurn.why: *Tú* plus the present *te sientas* gives the order.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, as a firm order: You will do as I say.
yourTurn.why: The future of *tú*, with *diga* after *lo que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, as a firm order to a child: You wait for me here.
yourTurn.why: *Me* comes before *esperas*, and the present *esperas* is the order.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the command into a flat order: *Quédate quieto.* Say: You stay still.
yourTurn.why: Take *tú* and the present, *te quedas*, instead of the imperative.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a group: *Harás lo que te diga.* Say: You all will do as I say.
yourTurn.answer: Ustedes harán lo que les diga.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, as a firm order to a girl: You stay calm.
yourTurn.why: A girl is *tranquila*, and the order is *tú te quedas*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Quedarse* in the sense of staying needs *te*.
Almost. After *lo que* the verb is *diga*, not *dices*.
Almost. To say "you" the verb ends in *-ás*, not *-á*.

personal: Think of a family joke, like telling a friend to sit down or go away, and say it as an order with *tú te…* or *harás…*.
